summary: Sheng Yen was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Dongchu (~1949–1977) and earned a doctorate at Rissho University (~1969–1975). He held posts at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1985–2009) and National Cheng Kung University.

Shenghai Li works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr. in 2012, and studied under Geshes Yeshe Thabkhe, Phuntsok Dhondup, Ngawang Sangye, and H. V. Nagaraja Rao.

Shenpen Hookham is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied under several traditional teachers, including Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche, and completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford in 1986 under Michael M. Broido.

Sheo Kumar Singh is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies under supervisor Satkari Mookerjee, with Kalidas Bhattacharyya and T. R. V. Murti serving as committee members.
Shi Huifeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (~2006–2011). He has held posts at the University of Hong Kong and as a professor at Fo Guang University (~2012).

Shichang Ma was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He was a researcher in Buddhist archaeology at the Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and held a post in Peking University's Archaeology Department beginning in 1982.
Shigeki Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held an assistant post at Kyoto University and served as an assistant professor at both Shuchiin University and Shitennoji University.
Shigeki Nagao is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed graduate studies at Otani University and served as a staff member at Kyoto Koka Women's University.

Shigeo Kamata was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo (~1962–1980), Aichi Gakuin University (~1988–1996), and ICPBS (~1996–2001), and directed Matsugaoka Bunko.
Shigeru Fukushima specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctorate in literature at Otani University (~2008–2013) under the supervision of Atsuyoshi Keika.

Shigeru Gorai was a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He held positions at Koyasan University (~1949–1964), Ryukoku University as lecturer, and Otani University as professor (~1964–1979).

Shigeru Matsumoto was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1956) and Harvard University (~1961–1967). He held academic posts at Tenri University (~1967–1978) and the University of the Sacred Heart (~1978–2003).

Shigeru Nakayama was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1951). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1960–1989) and Kanagawa University (~1989–1999).
Shigeru Shimizu was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1946 to 1949 and subsequently held a post there from ~1949 to 1989.
Shigetsu Sasaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts and under Sokatsu Shaku as a disciple around 1905. He founded the First Zen Institute of America in 1931.
Shili Xiong was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at China Inner Learning College in 1920 and held a post at Peking University from 1923 to 1955.
Shin Fujinaga is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Hiroshima University and as an associate professor at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College.
Shin Kitada is an Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He later held a post at the Eastern Institute.
Shin'ichi Endo is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a master's degree at Toyo University by ~1997, studying under Akira Suganuma.

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida. He taught at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University (1935–1949), Hanazono University (~1949), and was a visiting professor at Harvard University in 1958.
